title: Enhancing mathematics education for students with special educational needs through generative AI: A case study in Greece
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT can be used to create individualized mathematics lesson plans and worksheets that better support students with special educational needs. The authors frame the study around a new concept they call "mathematical familiarity," meaning the degree to which an AI-generated worksheet feels comfortable, relevant, and personally meaningful to a student.

The study reports a nine-hour teaching intervention in a Greek general education classroom. Two 8th-grade students, one diagnosed with dyslexia and one with autism spectrum disorder, received ChatGPT 3.5-generated worksheets tailored to their curriculum needs, interests, and hobbies. The worksheets were used alongside ordinary classroom teaching on square roots and irrational numbers, while the rest of the class used standard materials. Data came from classroom observation, student interviews, and a short e-questionnaire.

The authors conclude that the personalized ChatGPT worksheets increased engagement, helped the two students feel safe and confident, and supported their understanding of the target mathematics topics. They also report that the students performed well on class tests and expressed positive attitudes toward mathematics. The paper argues that generative AI can help teachers create differentiated materials more efficiently, but it also emphasizes the importance of teacher judgment, careful prompting, and training in the use of ChatGPT.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI generative AI chatbot/assistant based on GPT models that can generate text and support interactive prompting.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate individualized mathematics lesson plans and differentiated worksheets for two 8th grade students with special educational needs (dyslexia and ASD) in a general classroom.

findings.finding_summary: In a 9-hour qualitative teaching intervention with two 8th grade students with special educational needs, ChatGPT-generated worksheets were reported to help the students understand the square root of a positive number and irrational numbers. The authors report that both students completed classroom test exercises almost correctly and that the teacher observed improved engagement and interest; no effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Student understanding/performance on class worksheets and teacher-administered tests; interview and questionnaire responses about engagement and comfort

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study with two participants and no experimental control group, so causal evidence is limited. The paper does provide direct classroom observations, interviews, and student responses, but the methodology is descriptive rather than rigorous comparative evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported benefits are positive, but they are based on n=2 and no effect sizes are given, so the magnitude of impact cannot be quantified. The evidence suggests possible practical value for personalized math materials, but the strength of impact remains unclear.
